business_rules.statement: Rule one — one producer per record: exactly one surface creates each record type; every other surface reads, renders, or commands a change through the owning surface's own service.
business_rules.enforcement_point: the owning service rejects any write not carrying the owner's own rule set
business_rules.applies_to: every record type in the catalog

business_rules.statement: Operational data is created only in the Frontline Worker Application; no operational data originates in the Delivery Operations Hub itself.
business_rules.enforcement_point: create-call refusal plus an audit event on any other surface
business_rules.applies_to: all execution records below the Run

business_rules.statement: The Client Command Center authors nothing, owns no record, holds no configuration of its own and has no separate database; every action is a command executed through Delivery Operations Hub services.
Rule two — definition is pinned, execution is bound: a run pins its work package at assignment and executes that package for its whole life; the pin is immutable.
business_rules.applies_to: Run and every execution record beneath it

business_rules.statement: Rule three — the deterministic layer owns classification: detection is deterministic and runs on the worker's device; interpretation is agentic and runs afterwards.
business_rules.enforcement_point: on-device deterministic layer; no model in the deviation-triggering path

business_rules.statement: Every write commits the change and its audit event in one transaction; an action whose audit event cannot be committed does not happen.
business_rules.enforcement_point: one-transaction audit guarantee, rendered locked in settings with no off position for any account including the root

business_rules.statement: The platform has exactly one automatic transition: the run record's finish, executed by the platform run auto-close scheduler after the tenant finish window.
The user who creates a Job cannot approve that same Job; where the creator also holds the approver role the platform routes approval to a second qualified approver.
business_rules.enforcement_point: approval routing in the Job Lifecycle and Approval module

business_rules.statement: A tenant must hold an approver-capable role whenever a Job exists; without one the Job cannot leave pending_approval and no run can be created against it.
business_rules.enforcement_point: mandatory-role enforcement, surfaced as a configuration defect

business_rules.statement: Archiving a Site or Area auto-pauses every Job bound to it, notifies the Tenant Admin with the list, and prompts reassignment before archival completes; the cascade cannot silently strand a standing Job.

Re-parenting a Location (Cell) or changing hierarchy levels is blocked while in-flight Jobs exist; Area split, merge and re-parent are not supported at V1 and the sanctioned path is archive-and-recreate.
business_rules.enforcement_point: structural-change block; controls absent rather than disabled

business_rules.statement: A Severity 1 deviation always produces both a Deviation and a Hold, in every tenant; a Severity 2 deviation produces a Deviation and no Hold.
business_rules.enforcement_point: on-device deterministic classification at the instant of capture

business_rules.statement: Only a Quality Manager releases a hold, uniformly, with no exception by work type, risk class, or tag; the control is absent rather than disabled for every other role.
business_rules.enforcement_point: hold-release service and Client Command Center control rendering

business_rules.statement: Severity classification happens on the device at the instant of capture, including fully offline, with no server round-trip; server-side detection atoms are the mirror and confirmation path and are never the trigger.
business_rules.enforcement_point: packaged severity mappings and severity-catalog definitions in the work package

business_rules.statement: The Severity 1 floor is automatic lot freeze plus Quality-Manager-only release plus escalation; tenants may add actions and may never remove or weaken the floor, and the platform rejects rather than logs any attempt.
business_rules.enforcement_point: platform floor register rejection at entry

business_rules.statement: The hold lifecycle renders as issued, propagating, and in force per device, never as a single released state; each device's confirmation timestamp is listed.
The device reports capture state using thirteen distinct states and never reports a single state named synced.
Every Data Capture carries a pinned workflow version reference; a capture whose version reference is unknown to the server is quarantined rather than accepted.
Every capture event carries all nine envelope elements; a capture missing any element is quarantined rather than accepted.
Named-location provenance is recorded as configured site, line and cell names, never as a coordinate and never as a gate reading.
A device timestamp outside the tenant clock-skew threshold is not trusted to order writes; the event routes to human resolution and never orders a write.
The command channel carries exactly five classes and rejects any other command type; there is no real-time remote control of a worker mid-run.
No surface renders a command as applied before an acknowledgement is received from the device; expiry is explicit and never renders as success.
Attribution follows the logged-in identity and never the device, on every record, in every mode; a shared tablet confers nothing.
business_rules.enforcement_point: envelope construction and device session posture

business_rules.statement: Qualifications are supervisor-entered with full audit and never self-attested; a worker can never enter or amend their own qualification.
The qualification gate is the only configurable gate on the platform, with strict blocking as the default and notify-only as the floor; no silent posture exists.
business_rules.enforcement_point: tenant gate posture setting validated against the floor register

business_rules.statement: At expiry under strict posture the worker may complete the entire current run and the block applies only after that run ends, with no grace period beyond it.
A second clearance in the same Area on the same shift, regardless of worker, routes to the Quality Manager; the escalation scope is deliberately Area-level rather than per-worker.
Beyond the credential-trust window without contact, the device forces re-sync and blocks new work rather than trusting cached credentials or cached tenant state.
business_rules.applies_to: User account, Role grant, Scope grant, Qualification, Tenant state

business_rules.statement: Evidence media is never editable or deletable by any role or any artificial-intelligence capability, and never appears in the device gallery; it is written to the application's encrypted store.
business_rules.enforcement_point: evidence store and delete refusal with audit

business_rules.statement: Immutability is established at the point of capture rather than audited on afterwards; every correction is an appended record carrying who, when and what changed, and never alters an original.
business_rules.enforcement_point: commit-time immutability and append-only correction discipline
business_rules.applies_to: Data Capture, Step Execution, Evidence media

business_rules.statement: A capture arriving inside the finish window is accepted and flagged late_arrival; a capture arriving after finish is rejected as a capture and may only enter as an append-only correction under the audited-recompute rule.
business_rules.enforcement_point: finish window boundary at the run record

business_rules.statement: A cancelled run preserves partial step data, flags it as cancelled, and excludes it from the Execution Summary.
Exactly two in-flight modifications are permitted on a run: worker substitution and end-time extension within the tenant-configured cap.

No workflow version reaches published without a recorded Author, a distinct Reviewer, and a Release Authority, except through the labelled Lane B route which records its Command Center decision reference.
business_rules.enforcement_point: three-stage approval chain with separation of duties

business_rules.statement: Every republish requires a mandatory republish description stored in the permanent version history for every class; a notified-class version renders it as the worker-facing first-screen notice.
A version with incomplete locale coverage fails publication rather than shipping gaps to a floor; there is deliberately no partial-render fallback.
An in-progress run is never re-based by any publication of any class; scheduled-not-started runs get an explicit rebase-or-keep choice; completed runs are immutable.
A version is never auto-archived, including when all its Jobs are archived; archival is manual and deliberate against a clear no-active-Jobs indicator.
No authored content reaches a device except inside a version-pinned work package; Training Library content is excluded from the offline package and is never required mid-run.
A package carries the severity-catalog definitions and tenant action bundles needed to classify and act at capture, so classification never requires a server.
An artificial-intelligence-drafted difficulty level cannot be published without passing the full review chain; the platform's artificial intelligence may accelerate authoring but never publishes.
Nothing is machine-translated at runtime on any surface; coaching and instruction content render from authored variants per locale.
Only in-app and email channels exist at V1, platform-wide, at every tier; in-app notifications cannot be muted by any role.

A notification must never be the only mechanism enforcing safety, a hold, a qualification, an authorization, an approval, a suspension, or a device command; enforcement lives in the record and on the device.
business_rules.enforcement_point: architecture separation of enforcement from notification

business_rules.statement: Acknowledgement and resolution are distinct, timestamped states, and fallback deliveries are visibly marked.
There is exactly one digest service per shift; users may mute sections but never the service.
Reports always carry a data-as-of timestamp and are never presented as real-time; late data materially changing delivered figures is flagged as a correction in the next delivery.
business_rules.applies_to: Report data set and Saved report format

business_rules.statement: An all-tenant broadcast cannot be sent without Root Super Admin approval; single-tenant notices are routine Admin actions.
No atom or agent can be enabled while any gating scenario is pending or failing, for any account including the root; the evaluation gate has no off position.
business_rules.applies_to: Atom registration record and Agent definition

business_rules.statement: No agent runs on a device, and no model sits anywhere in the deviation-triggering path; detection-class atoms implement rule-based logic only.
business_rules.enforcement_point: device build contains no model runtime

business_rules.statement: Memory is isolated absolutely per tenant; nothing is shared across tenants and no tenant data becomes external training data.
Profile memory holds aggregates only and never a raw per-worker behavioural feed.
An artificial-intelligence output never becomes an effect except through a human gate or pre-authorised, Studio-authored policy approved at publication.
business_rules.enforcement_point: governance binding on the agent record

business_rules.statement: An emergency pause parks agents at stage boundaries, leaves raised gates human-decidable, and leaves the on-device deterministic layer entirely untouched; the deterministic backbone has no off switch.
Exactly three platform access classes exist and no console path reaches record-level tenant content outside one of them; no ambient browsing exists anywhere on the console.
A normal support session has no write capability of any kind and is read-only without exception; the tenant can end it at any moment from its banner.

The compliance-emergency path is the only route with write capability into tenant data and the only entry into a compliance-suspended tenant; it requires a named emergency class plus two authorisations, the Root Super Admin and one Admin.
business_rules.enforcement_point: dual authorisation and declared scope before opening

business_rules.statement: A looser-than-floor configuration value is rejected at entry with the bound stated and is never stored; the register rejects, it does not log. Tenants tighten; they never loosen.
business_rules.enforcement_point: platform floor register at the point of entry

business_rules.statement: Nothing is purged: the tenant-set retention value is a hot-retrievability horizon, data beyond it tiers and remains retrievable, and deletion occurs only where a named compliance standard requires it.
A legal hold in force prevents tiering and compliance-driven deletion for its scope; both placement and release are dual-approved critical-class actions.
business_rules.enforcement_point: lifecycle schedulers check the hold first

business_rules.statement: Every platform-side access event against a tenant appears in that tenant's own audit stream and in the tenant's Platform Access History screen.
business_rules.enforcement_point: mirroring obligation on all three access classes

business_rules.statement: Anonymisation is the platform's one irreversible act: worker name and identity anonymise at 24 months for standard commercial tenants and never in Regulated-Industry mode; measurement, result and evidence survive.
business_rules.applies_to: Worker record (OBJ-028) and worker personal data

business_rules.statement: Every occurrence carries an idempotency key and no effect executes twice for one key; exactly one process may hold a lease on an occurrence and a write carrying a stale fencing token is rejected.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Effect Receipt idempotency check and fencing token validation

business_rules.statement: No retry policy is unbounded and no backfill executes outside its declared blast-radius bounds; every exhausted occurrence lands in a dead-letter record rather than being retried again or silently dropped.
No implementation artifact in the scheduled-work area is named 'job'; a Scheduled Occurrence is never the AVIIXA Job object OBJ-013.
business_rules.enforcement_point: naming lint on the scheduled-work implementation

business_rules.statement: A scheduler failure leaves the affected work undone and visible and never produces a silent completion — a run stays complete past its window rather than finishing silently.
business_rules.enforcement_point: platform-health incident raised instead of a silent finish
business_rules.applies_to: run auto-close scheduler and the other three schedulers

business_rules.statement: Every Job and every Workflow carries exactly one Job Type, and the eight platform-seeded types are read-only in every workspace; a Job cannot be created without exactly one Job Type.
business_rules.enforcement_point: refusal rather than a default value

business_rules.statement: A Service Type tag never blocks, enforces or decides any platform behaviour; the tag suggests and never decides, and removing it changes no qualification requirement already stated on the Job.
A Shift inherits its Site's timezone; no per-Area or per-Shift timezone override is offered at V1, and editing a Shift never retroactively re-stamps completed runs.
No tier record carries price metadata and no platform surface computes an invoice; there is no payment integration, no invoicing and no pricing engine at any tier.
business_rules.enforcement_point: tier record schema and commercial boundary
business_rules.applies_to: Tier Record (OBJ-003) and Usage Ledger Entry (OBJ-004)

business_rules.statement: A Tenant Group is never rendered in any tenant-facing surface and carries no operational behaviour at V1.
business_rules.enforcement_point: tenant-facing endpoints return no group reference

business_rules.statement: The Frontline Worker Application deliberately never shows pace, timers or performance state, and contains no reporting or dashboards by design.
No worker may override a gate that blocks them; the worker never sees a release control.
The specification gate is hard and platform-fixed with no tenant off switch; a failed specification capture blocks progression and no author or tenant setting can configure that away.
A soft proof gate permits advance while recording the missing proof as an evidence gap; a hard gate blocks advance.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Screen Section 4 gate and proof configuration

business_rules.statement: Every object card states artificial-intelligence read access and write access separately, and no card grants an artificial-intelligence capability write access to evidence, audit, holds, or classification.
Where a facet genuinely does not apply, the card says Not applicable and gives the specific reason; no facet is ever left blank and no permission matrix cell is blank.
business_rules.enforcement_point: TEST-DOM-003 fails the build on any card missing a facet

business_rules.statement: Genealogy at launch is one level of as-built links plus the full rework history, append-only and repeatable; the walkable multi-level tree and downstream-consumer hold propagation are defined later extensions.
business_rules.applies_to: As-built genealogy link and Rework cycle record

business_rules.statement: The rework loop supports unlimited cycles, each fully readable, with nothing overwritten; the model has no cycle limit and imposes none.
Everything executes as a run: where a tenant does not schedule explicitly, the platform auto-creates a single implicit run so the record of truth never has a run-shaped hole in it.
The platform enforces no review service-level agreement; aging highlights and the digest are the pressure, not a lock, so a review backlog is visible rather than blocking.
Lane A self-tunes selection and ranking preferences and changes no configured value by definition; Lane B is anything a human configured and never changes without a person.
business_rules.applies_to: Feedback signal record and Lane-B learning proposal

business_rules.statement: The platform never invents content, rules, or thresholds; where the source leaves a concept contested the source's own wording is used with the decision identifier attached rather than a coined term.

decisions.question: Is the Site level a mandatory minimum or a recommended minimum in the operational hierarchy?
options: §2.1: Site-as-required-minimum is an open drafting value and recommended
decisions.adopted_working_position: the Site level is mandatory and a default Site is auto-created at tenant provisioning, so the rule is satisfied literally without onboarding friction
decisions.status: adopted working position, taken 2026-08-14, Derived Clarification not SoW Fact
decisions.impact: Determines whether onboarding must create a Site before any Area, Shift or Job.

decisions.question: Does a Job bind to a single Area, or to one parent node at the tenant's configured depth?
options: §4.5.1: a Job carries its single Area binding — one Area per Job is a hard constraint
§2.1: one parent node per Job at the tenant's configured depth
decisions.adopted_working_position: §2.1's reading — a Job anchors at the deepest parent node its tenant configured; Part II is a platform-wide contract no surface may fork
decisions.status: adopted working position, taken 2026-08-14, Derived Clarification
decisions.impact: Decides whether a Job may anchor at a Location (Cell).

decisions.question: Are the finish-window bounds settled at 24 hours to 7 days, or still an open drafting value?
options: §2.4: bounds are an open drafting value suggesting 24 hours to 7 days
§4.6.8 and §8.7.4: settled at a floor of 24 hours and a ceiling of 7 days
decisions.status: open; both readings preserved; modelled as a bounded tenant setting validated against the floor register
decisions.impact: Sets the validated bound on the tenant's record-finish window.

decisions.question: What state does a manually closed stuck run stand in at close?
options: §6.2.6: the run stands submitted with the gap recorded
§2.4: the run is complete at close time
decisions.status: open; neither reading adopted; the finish-window clock behaviour is common to both
decisions.impact: Governs the recorded state of every supervisor manual close.

decisions.question: Is submitted a per-worker event or a run-level state, and what triggers complete?
decisions.status: open; raised in Chapter 5, Section 5.16
decisions.impact: Rewrites the three closing-state glossary entries and every chapter using the words.

decisions.question: Does an approved Lane B proposal auto-publish a patch version outside the three-stage approval chain?
options: §5.11.1: no Workflow content reaches the frontline without explicit human sign-off at each of the three stages
§5.16.3 and §6.7.4: an approved Lane B proposal auto-publishes a patch version with no second approval, no ceremony
decisions.status: open; carried unresolved; modelled as a distinct, audited, visibly marked publication route into published
decisions.impact: Decides whether a second publication route into published exists.

decisions.question: Who may decide a Lane B proposal below Quality Manager?
options: a named Lane B decider below Quality Manager
decisions.status: open; no term invented for a Lane B decider below Quality Manager
decisions.impact: Decides the minimum authority for learned-change approval.

decisions.question: Which capture types does the platform support, given §1.7 disagrees with §5.5.3?
decisions.adopted_working_position: the seven types are measurement entry, photo capture, barcode or Quick Response code scan, checkbox confirmation, digital signature, free text, and dropdown selection, plus none for instruction-only screens; dropdown selection is a launch type; checkbox confirmation carries a multiplicity setting
decisions.status: adopted working position, open for client ratification; §1.7 against §5.5.3 disagreement remains recorded
decisions.impact: A player cannot render a capture type the contract does not name.

decisions.question: Is pre-authorised policy a form of gating or an exception to it, and is the Prevention Agent gated at runtime?
options: §3.7 and §6.6.1: the Prevention Agent operates entirely under pre-authorised Studio-authored policy; the runtime gate exists only beyond it
§8.3.2 and §8.3.3: action agents change state and every one routes through a human gate; Prevention Agent labelled action, gated
decisions.adopted_working_position: gating is declared per agent in the agent record's governance-binding field, so a Gate item arises only where a proposal exceeds the proposing agent's pre-authorised policy; the Prevention Agent is bound to authoring-time policy and the Shift Handoff Agent to none — reasoning agent
decisions.status: adopted working position, taken 2026-08-14, open for client ratification
decisions.impact: Determines whether every Prevention Agent output raises a gate item.

decisions.question: Who administers the platform-seeded Job Type catalog in Super Admin?
decisions.status: open; carried unresolved
decisions.impact: Leaves seeded-catalog administration authority undefined.

decisions.question: What are the canonical names and codes of the eight seeded Job Types and eight seeded Service Type tags?
decisions.adopted_working_position: the platform-seeded catalogue ships empty at version 1 and every tenant creates its own Job Types and Service Type tags immediately on every tier; the sixteen names remain owed by the client and are never invented
decisions.status: adopted working position, taken 2026-08-14, open for client ratification
decisions.impact: Determines the shipped taxonomy content and tenant onboarding effort.

decisions.question: How are global taxonomy versioning, deprecation, replacement and archival handled?
decisions.status: open; carried unresolved
decisions.impact: Leaves seeded-taxonomy lifecycle undefined.

decisions.question: Which fields are package-borne and which are server-only?
options: field-by-field assignment carried in the package contract of Part VII, which does not enumerate it
decisions.status: open; carried unresolved
decisions.impact: Decides what the device can evaluate alone.

decisions.question: Does the work package carry all three work-instruction difficulty levels or only the assigned worker's?
decisions.status: open; the package definition carries all levels until it resolves
decisions.impact: Affects package size and device storage pressure.

decisions.question: What happens to an in-flight run whose Content Library item changes mid-run, given pointers propagate immediately but packages are pinned?
options: §5.7: screens hold pointers so a library edit propagates to every referencing screen immediately
§5.14 and Part II: a run's work package is pinned at assignment and never re-based
decisions.status: open; both readings preserved on the affected cards
decisions.impact: Governs containment checklist and coaching asset behaviour mid-run.

decisions.question: Does the device or the Deviation and Containment Agent launch the pre-authorised containment checklist?
options: Option A: §3.4 and §7.9.1 layer b — the device launches it locally at classification
decisions.adopted_working_position: Option A: the device launches the pre-authorised containment checklist locally, from the version-pinned work package, at the instant of classification, with no network required; the Deviation and Containment Agent enriches the deviation brief afterwards and never triggers the checklist
decisions.status: adopted working position, taken 2026-08-14 because it is the safer reading; source disagreement stays recorded at section 51.11A
decisions.impact: Every checklist step must be renderable from the package with no server call.

decisions.question: On reconnection, does a device upload captures first or pull commands first?
decisions.adopted_working_position: stop-class commands are pulled and applied first, then every pending capture uploads with nothing discarded, then the enabling-class commands apply
decisions.status: adopted working position, open for client ratification; the source explicitly defers payload and ordering semantics to the Frontline functional specification
decisions.impact: Sets the reconnection ordering contract for every device.

decisions.question: How long may a wipe command remain pending, and what happens if the device never returns?
decisions.status: open; carried unresolved
decisions.impact: A device wipe requires a final sync attempt an offline device cannot perform.

decisions.question: What is the device behaviour under storage pressure?
options: explicitly deferred to the Frontline functional specification; no behaviour may be invented
decisions.status: open; carried unresolved
decisions.impact: Governs evidence capture when a device runs out of space.

decisions.question: What are the entity fields, keys and lot-formation rules of the unit model?
options: gated on the owed engineering paper Traceability_Unit_Model_Solution_v0.1
decisions.status: open; carried unresolved
decisions.impact: Blocks the data-model appendix and field-level unit modelling.

decisions.question: Which surface creates the Lot record and who may edit it?
options: Assumption: lot definition is tenant configuration in the tenant administration area and lot instances are bound at capture by the Frontline Worker Application, with the Delivery Operations Hub as system of record
decisions.status: raised here as a new Client Decision Required
decisions.impact: A Severity 1 freeze targets this object; an object with no named creator has no named authority.

decisions.question: Is the Execution Summary a computed view or a stored document?
options: §4.7.1: a computed view, not a stored document
§4.7.4 and §4.7.5: prior computed output is preserved and a PDF carries an audit hash, implying stored snapshots
decisions.status: raised here as a new Client Decision Required; modelled as a computed view with immutable computation snapshots retained at each recompute
decisions.impact: Decides whether Summary snapshots are stored artifacts.

decisions.question: Do Plant Manager and Quality Director exist as roles?
options: §3.5: there is no Quality Director and the five roles are fixed
§6.1.3 lists Plant Manager / Quality Director as a Command Center user group; §5.18 lists Plant Manager in a table headed Fixed role
decisions.status: open; carried unresolved
decisions.impact: Affects landing views and escalation-fallback duties.

decisions.question: What ordering does the plus notation in Supervisor+ and QM+ imply across five additive, non-hierarchical roles?
options: no ordering is defined by the source
decisions.status: open; carried unresolved
decisions.impact: Every authority matrix using 'Supervisor and above' is ambiguous.

decisions.question: How is the naming divergence for the Delivery Operations Hub carried?
decisions.status: carried in the decision canon
decisions.impact: Governs surface naming across the blueprint.

decisions.question: What is the escalation fallback when nobody holding the target role is on shift?
options: escalate to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, marked visibly as a fallback
decisions.status: open; §3.9 records it as an open drafting value
decisions.impact: Determines who receives a Severity 1 escalation when the roster is empty.

decisions.question: What triggers exit from soft suspension, given there is no payment integration?
options: §4.2.4: soft suspension lifts on the operator's signal and not on a payment event
§8.9.2 and Part IX: soft state exit is automatic on payment / soft clears on payment
decisions.adopted_working_position: release by an explicit operator signal in the Super Admin platform console, with no payment event observed and the payment-integration path left open and unbuilt
decisions.status: adopted working position 2026-08-14, open for client ratification
decisions.impact: Removes any payment-event trigger from the tenant-state machine.

decisions.question: Does the 24-month anonymisation model stand unchanged under the no-purge lifecycle?
decisions.status: open; carried unresolved
decisions.impact: Governs worker personal data treatment at 24 months.

decisions.question: What is the archived-data retrieval expectation — minutes, hours, or the next business day?
decisions.status: open; carried unresolved
decisions.impact: An audit question about tiered data that deserves a written answer.

decisions.question: Which named compliance standards mandate deletion under the no-purge model?
decisions.status: open; the no-purge model's one dependency
decisions.impact: Deletion occurs only where a named standard requires it.

decisions.question: Which sections does the per-shift digest carry?
options: the union of both digest section lists
decisions.status: open; raised in Chapter 5, Section 5.16
decisions.impact: Changes digest configuration across the Hub and Tenant Administration chapters.

decisions.question: What is the exact worker-facing wording of the compliance-suspension message, in both locales?
decisions.status: open; raised in Chapter 5, Section 5.16
decisions.impact: Determines the fixed on-device compliance stop message.

decisions.question: Does segregation of duties apply to recurrence modification as it does to Job creation and approval?
options: Assumption: the same rule applies because §4.5.4 says the change passes the same Quality-Manager approval gate as the Job itself
decisions.status: raised here as a new Client Decision Required not present in the canon's contradiction register
decisions.impact: Decides whether a proposer of a recurrence change may approve it.

decisions.question: What happens to a defective published Workflow version already on a tablet — is there any rollback?
options: publish a corrective version and use notified-class adoption machinery, leaving the defective version permanently readable
decisions.status: raised here as a new Client Decision Required; Recommendation — Research and Development
decisions.impact: A tenant under a quality regime will ask what happens to a bad instruction already on a tablet.

decisions.question: Who owns device enrollment and lifecycle — the Super Admin console or the tenant?
options: §7.5.2: device enrollment and lifecycle are Super Admin's
§8.13.4: enrollment operations are tenant self-service with the console keeping the policy layer, cross-tenant telemetry and wipe authority
decisions.status: raised here as a new Client Decision Required; the chapter splits the object's authority explicitly rather than choosing
decisions.impact: Determines who enrolls and retires tablets.

decisions.question: What is the standardised device profile?
decisions.status: open; carried unresolved
decisions.impact: Bounds the published minimum device specification.

decisions.question: What is the fixed category list for anomalies, which the source specifies but never enumerates?
options: enumerate it platform-side as part of severity governance
make it tenant-configurable within platform bounds
derive it from the deviation mechanisms
decisions.status: raised here as a new Client Decision Required; recommendation is a platform-defined list extendable by tenants above it
decisions.impact: A fixed list nobody has written is not implementable.

decisions.question: What is the canonical identity of the five standard report data sets, given set 4 is named differently in two clauses?
decisions.status: open; the identity of all five sets remains owed by the client
decisions.impact: Determines report data set naming and scope.

decisions.question: How are composed agents deprecated, disabled or rolled back, and what happens to their in-flight runs?
decisions.status: open; carried unresolved
decisions.impact: Leaves composed-agent lifecycle and in-flight run fate undefined.

decisions.question: What happens when trace writing fails during an agent run?
options: treat an untraceable agent run as a failed run and do not deliver its output
decisions.status: raised here as a new Client Decision Required; Recommendation — Research and Development
decisions.impact: Prevents an unexplainable agent effect at the cost of agent availability.

decisions.question: Are platform-side tenant current-value changes, including feature enablement, Admin actions or Platform Engineer changes requiring Admin approval?
options: §8.2.2: atom enablement is a Platform Engineer change requiring Admin approval
§8.19: platform-side tenant current-value changes including feature enablement are Admin actions
decisions.status: open; carried unresolved
decisions.impact: Sets the approval class for enabling capabilities per tenant.

decisions.question: What export-control commitment (International Traffic in Arms Regulations, Export Administration Regulations) applies, and does it collide with the granted-access operating model?
options: nothing export-control-flavoured is committed before the client's answer lands
decisions.status: open; carried unresolved
decisions.impact: A genuine export-control commitment implies operations and topology that collide with granted access.

decisions.question: How are platform rollouts governed within the change-approval queue's scope?
decisions.status: open; listed as attaching to the change-approval queue's scope
decisions.impact: Affects staged platform change delivery.

decisions.question: Should scheduled-work objects be rendered as a Super Admin platform console view with no tenant-facing surface?
options: render a console view showing definitions, upcoming occurrences, recent attempts, dead-lettered items and the reconciliation position
decisions.status: open; Recommendation — Research and Development
decisions.impact: Makes the promise that upcoming lifecycle events are surfaced before they run checkable.

decisions.question: Are schedule changes engineering-class or critical-class, given two of the four schedulers execute critical-class effects?
decisions.status: open; recommendation is critical-class for any schedule whose effect is critical-class
decisions.impact: Approval authority for changing when data is anonymised.

decisions.question: What is the misfire policy when a scheduled moment passes without the work running?
decisions.status: open; recommendation is per-definition policy with run-once-on-recovery as the default
decisions.impact: Skipping a run auto-close is wrong; catching up two hundred anonymisation windows may be unsafe.

decisions.question: May a new occurrence start while the prior one still runs (overlap policy)?
decisions.status: open; skip-if-running recommended
decisions.impact: Prevents concurrent execution of the same scheduled work.

decisions.question: What are the idempotency key definition and the Effect Receipt's exact semantics?
decisions.status: open; recommendation is a compound key of definition, occurrence and subject
decisions.impact: Anonymisation is irreversible; a duplicate anonymisation of a different cohort would be unrecoverable.

decisions.question: What are the retry and back-off limits and the dead-letter threshold?
options: exponential back-off with a per-definition attempt ceiling
decisions.status: open; a bounded policy is mandatory rather than optional
decisions.impact: The platform must never enter an infinite retry loop.

decisions.question: What are the scheduler lease duration and fencing-token semantics?
decisions.status: open; recommendation is renewal-based leases with a per-definition ceiling
decisions.impact: A lease shorter than the longest legitimate execution causes duplicate claims.

decisions.question: What are the per-scheduler Recovery Time and Recovery Point Objectives, and what happens if the run auto-close scheduler fails?
options: hold the run in complete, raise a platform incident, and finish on scheduler recovery with the original window boundary preserved as the effective finish time
decisions.status: open; recommendation is per-scheduler objectives; also covers the run auto-close scheduler-failure behaviour raised in 7.3.1
decisions.impact: The effective finish time affects late-data acceptance.

decisions.question: What approval authority governs a Replay or Backfill Request?
options: approval class inherited from the underlying effect
decisions.status: open; recommendation is inheritance from the effect, so a backfill of anonymisation is critical-class
decisions.impact: A backfill can produce a large number of irreversible effects at once.

decisions.question: What is the reconciliation cadence and who may act on a discrepancy?
decisions.status: open; recommendation is continuous reconciliation with alerting for critical-class effects and daily otherwise
decisions.impact: An undetected anonymisation gap is a compliance exposure; a run auto-close gap is a data-integrity exposure.

contradictions.description: Site level: §2.1 marks Site-as-required-minimum an open drafting value and recommends it; §4.3.1 states flatly that the Site level is mandatory.
Job binding: §2.1 says one parent node per Job at the tenant's configured depth; §4.5.1 says one Area per Job is a hard constraint. They differ materially for a tenant configuring Cell depth.
conflicting_values: one parent node per Job at configured depth (§2.1)
one Area per Job, hard constraint (§4.5.1)

contradictions.description: Finish-window bounds: §2.4 marks them an open drafting value suggesting 24 hours to 7 days; §4.6.8 and §8.7.4 state them settled at a 24-hour floor and a 7-day ceiling.
conflicting_values: open drafting value, suggested 24 hours to 7 days

contradictions.description: Manually closed stuck run: §6.2.6 says the run stands submitted with the gap recorded; §2.4 says it is complete at close time. Neither reading is adopted.
Lane B publication: §5.11.1 requires explicit human sign-off at each of three stages; §5.16.3 and §6.7.4 have an approved Lane B proposal auto-publish a patch with no second approval, no ceremony.
Capture types: the seven capture types are named differently in §7.8.3 and §5.5.3; a player cannot render a type the contract does not name.

Agent gating: §3.7 and §6.6.1 say the Prevention Agent runs entirely under pre-authorised policy with a runtime gate only beyond it; §8.3.2 says every action agent routes through a human gate, and §8.3.3 labels the Prevention Agent 'action, gated'.
conflicting_values: gate exists only beyond pre-authorised policy (§3.7, §6.6.1)
every action agent is gated at runtime (§8.3.2, §8.3.3)

contradictions.description: Containment checklist launch: §3.4 and §7.9.1 layer b place the launch on the device at classification; §5.2.2 and §5.7.1 place it on the Deviation and Containment Agent.
conflicting_values: device launches locally at classification (§3.4, §7.9.1 layer b)

contradictions.description: Soft suspension exit: §4.2.4 says it lifts on the operator's signal and not on a payment event, and §4.2.1 and §8.12 state there is no payment integration; §8.9.2 and Part IX say soft clears automatically on payment.

Execution Summary nature: §4.7.1 states it is a computed view, not a stored document; §4.7.4 requires the prior computed output be preserved and §4.7.5 exports a PDF carrying an audit hash — both implying stored snapshots.
conflicting_values: computed view, not a stored document (§4.7.1)
prior computed output preserved plus hashed PDF (§4.7.4, §4.7.5)

contradictions.description: Roles: §3.5 says there is no Quality Director and fixes five roles; §6.1.3 lists 'Plant Manager / Quality Director' as a Command Center user group and §5.18 lists Plant Manager under a heading 'Fixed role'.
conflicting_values: five fixed roles, no Quality Director (§3.5)
Plant Manager / Quality Director as user groups and fixed roles (§6.1.3, §5.18)

contradictions.description: Plus notation: authority matrices use 'Supervisor and above' and 'Quality Manager and above' without defining an ordering across five additive, non-hierarchical roles.
conflicting_values: ordering implied by the plus notation
five additive, non-hierarchical roles with no ordering defined

contradictions.description: Device ownership: §7.5.2 states device enrollment and lifecycle are Super Admin's; §8.13.4 states enrollment operations are tenant self-service with the console keeping policy, telemetry and wipe authority.
conflicting_values: Super Admin owns enrollment and lifecycle (§7.5.2)
tenant self-service enrollment, console keeps policy (§8.13.4)

contradictions.description: Report data set naming: §4.10.5 names set 4 'Clearance (qualification-override) frequency by role' while §6.12.1 names it 'Override frequency by role'.

Feature enablement authority: §8.2.2 makes atom enablement a Platform Engineer change requiring Admin approval; §8.19 makes platform-side tenant current-value changes, including feature enablement, Admin actions.
conflicting_values: Platform Engineer change requiring Admin approval (§8.2.2)

contradictions.description: Content Library pointers versus package pinning: §5.7 propagates a library edit immediately to every referencing screen; §5.14 and Part II pin the run's package at assignment and never re-base it.
conflicting_values: package pinned and never re-based (§5.14, Part II)

contradictions.description: Reconnection ordering: safety argues stop-class commands must land before more work happens; data integrity argues unsynced captures must never be risked. The source defers payload and ordering semantics to the Frontline functional specification.
Package-borne versus server-only fields: §6.7.4 says the authoritative field-by-field assignment is carried in the package contract of Part VII, and Part VII does not enumerate it.
conflicting_values: Part VII does not enumerate it

contradictions.description: Anomaly category list: the source specifies 'a fixed category list' for anomalies but never enumerates it; a fixed list that nobody has written is not implementable.
conflicting_values: a fixed category list is specified

contradictions.description: Device wipe: the sync-then-wipe rule requires a final sync attempt before erasure, which an offline device cannot perform; the source states neither how long a wipe may remain pending nor what happens if the device never returns.
conflicting_values: wipe requires a final sync attempt
an offline device cannot perform it and no timeout is stated

contradictions.description: Semantic memory precedence: the source states curated ingestion plus agents write the semantic store without stating precedence; curation-wins is the only reading consistent with 'the platform never invents content'.
Location (Cell) archival cascade: the source states the archival cascade for Sites and Areas only, not for Cells; the same soft-archive treatment is assumed pending confirmation.
conflicting_values: cascade stated for Sites and Areas

contradictions.description: Recurrence-change segregation of duties: the source states segregation of duties for Job creation and approval but does not restate it explicitly for recurrence modification.
conflicting_values: same rule applies because it is the same gate (§4.5.4)

contradictions.description: Recovery Time Objective and Recovery Point Objective are unstated across record reconciliation, Hub service availability, hold-release propagation, package delivery, agent health, lifecycle schedulers and every scheduler; no value is invented.
conflicting_values: the Statement of Work states none

failures_fallbacks.trigger: register drift — a short form used in a chapter that is not in the abbreviation register, or silent term invention for a contested concept
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: the short form is added to the register and expanded in place; the term is admitted with an honest classification and the decision identifier attached
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: where the short form is a source term with no agreed full name, the source's own wording is quoted verbatim and the gap recorded
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: an awkward but accurate phrase, never a clean but misleading one; no unexplained short form survives in narrative prose
failures_fallbacks.recovery: re-issue of the chapter and a sweep of every chapter using the term

failures_fallbacks.trigger: a non-owning surface attempts a direct write, or a device commits a record whose owning service later rejects it
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: the write is refused at the boundary with the owning rule stated; a rejected capture is marked quarantined rather than accepted
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: where the device timestamp lies outside the clock-skew threshold, the event routes to human resolution and is never auto-ordered
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: the operational record stands with the disputed value quarantined and visibly flagged, the run blocked where a gate depends on it, and no summary computed from a disputed value
failures_fallbacks.recovery: the accepted value is written as an append-only record with full attribution; the Summary recomputes under the audited-recompute rule with the prior output preserved

failures_fallbacks.trigger: device loses power mid-capture; upload interrupted; server rejects a capture whose pinned version reference is unknown; a Unit Execution opened against a serial already closed on another device
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: the capture stays committed locally and the upload retries on the next sync opportunity; the sync indicator shows the pending count honestly
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: a Supervisor may close a stuck run as an audited act with a mandatory note, after which the run stands submitted with the gap recorded
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: the run finishes with the gap explicitly recorded; no figure is presented as complete when it is not
failures_fallbacks.recovery: captures land on reconnection and the affected numbers recompute; late captures inside the finish window fold in flagged late_arrival

failures_fallbacks.trigger: the owning service is unavailable when a Client Command Center decision is taken
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: the decision is not recorded as taken and the surface reports the failure rather than showing an applied state
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: the same decision is available from the owning Delivery Operations Hub screen; where both entry points are unavailable the decision waits
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: the floor stays safe because the strictest state persists locally; a Severity 1 hold remains in force because it was placed by the on-device deterministic layer
failures_fallbacks.recovery: the decision is retaken and recorded once the owning service returns; no duplicate decision may be recorded

failures_fallbacks.trigger: the actor lacks authority; the source state is not the state the actor saw; the audit write fails
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: the transition is refused with the current state stated, never applied optimistically
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: where no approver-capable role holder exists, the Job cannot leave pending_approval — a configuration defect the platform must surface
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: the record remains in its prior state, and where that state blocks execution, execution stays blocked
failures_fallbacks.recovery: the transition is retried once the authority or state condition is met; the refused attempt appears as an audit entry

failures_fallbacks.trigger: a device never returns; a worker leaves site mid-run; the run auto-close scheduler does not fire; a capture arrives after finish
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: the run stays in Submitted with the gap visible in the freshness marker rather than being reported complete
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: if the scheduler fails the run does not silently finish; it remains complete past its window and the condition is a platform-health incident
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: a run that finishes with a recorded gap, never a run that reports complete data it does not hold
failures_fallbacks.recovery: the device returns and delivers; captures inside the window fold in flagged; audited recompute preserves the prior output

failures_fallbacks.trigger: no second approver exists; the parent location is archived while in-flight Jobs exist; approval routing cannot resolve a role holder
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: the Job stays in pending_approval and the condition is surfaced to the Tenant Admin
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: the Job cannot become active; no run can be created against it; the floor executes nothing unreviewed
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: an unapproved Job that produces no work — the correct outcome
failures_fallbacks.recovery: approval by a qualified second person after the Tenant Admin grants the approver role, itself audited

failures_fallbacks.trigger: a mis-classified bump reaches review; locale coverage incomplete at publish; a published version later found defective; a device holds a package version the server no longer recognises
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: publication fails rather than shipping gaps; the version returns to Draft with the reason recorded
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: a defect found after publication is corrected by a new version through the same chain — no edit-in-place, no unpublish; safety-bearing defects use the version-change command class or suspension, neither instant
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: the in-flight run completes on its pinned version and its record states which version it executed
failures_fallbacks.recovery: the corrective version publishes and adopts; the linkage view shows which Jobs and Runs sat on which version

failures_fallbacks.trigger: escalation cannot be delivered because nobody holding the role is on shift; a sibling device never reconnects; the release command is lost; the containment checklist references a library item the package does not carry
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: the nobody-on-shift default escalates to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, marked visibly as a fallback delivery
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: unacknowledged Critical notifications re-notify after 4 hours, tightened to 1 hour in Regulated-Industry mode; a notification must never be the only mechanism enforcing a hold
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: the lot stays frozen — a frozen lot with a delayed escalation is correct; an unfrozen lot with a delivered notification is not
failures_fallbacks.recovery: devices reconnect and confirm; the release, once issued, reaches each device at its next sync; propagation lag is recorded as telemetry

failures_fallbacks.trigger: the device never returns; the command is superseded by a later command of the same class; the device rejects the command as invalid; the command expires
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: the command remains queued and the surface continues to show it as not applied
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: a superseding command replaces it and both are retained; the command expires with an explicit expired state, never silently and never as success
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: the strictest of the current device state and the pending command persists; for a release this means the restriction stands
failures_fallbacks.recovery: the device returns, pulls in order, and acknowledges; the per-device package inventory and propagation-lag telemetry reconcile intent against effect

failures_fallbacks.trigger: a surface chapter or an implementation introduces an object not present in the catalog, or contradicts a card
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: the new object is added to the catalog with a full card and a classification rather than being carried privately in one surface
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: where the addition contradicts a stated source fact, the contradiction is raised as a DEC-* item with both readings preserved rather than resolved by the implementer
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: the implementation does not proceed on the contested object; other objects are unaffected because the catalog is decomposed
failures_fallbacks.recovery: the decision lands and the card is updated with its source classification changed accordingly

failures_fallbacks.trigger: tenant state cannot be evaluated at a surface, or the usage ledger falls behind
